message.content:
Below is a concise overview of the key rights and protections you have as a residential tenant in Texas.  (For the most up‑to‑date information, you can always consult the Texas Property Code or a local attorney.)

| # | Right / Protection | What it Means | Typical Practical Tips |
|---|--------------------|---------------|------------------------|
| **1** | **Security Deposit Limits** | Landlords may charge a maximum of **one month’s rent** for a single‑unit dwelling and **two months’ rent** for a multi‑unit building. | Keep a copy of the lease and any receipt for the deposit. |
| **2** | **Deposit Return** | Landlord must return the deposit (minus any lawful deductions) within **30 days** after you move out, unless you and the landlord agree otherwise. | Request a written itemized list of deductions if the landlord keeps part of the deposit. |
| **3** | **Habitability / Repairs** | Landlord must keep the premises in a safe, sanitary condition and make necessary repairs. | Report problems in writing; keep copies of all communications. |
| **4** | **Notice Requirements for Repairs** | If you report a repair issue, the landlord has **10 days** to fix it. | If the landlord fails to act, you may withhold rent or take other legal steps. |
| **5** | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | Landlord cannot disturb your peaceful use of the property. | Document any disturbances (e.g., noise, entry without notice). |
| **6** | **Entry Notice** | Landlord must give **24 hours’ written notice** before entering, except in emergencies. | Keep a log of all entries; request a copy of the notice if you suspect a violation. |
| **7** | **Eviction Process** | Landlord must follow the Texas Eviction Procedure (notice, court filing, judgment). | If you receive an eviction notice, respond promptly and consider seeking legal advice. |
| **8** | **Rent Increase Notice** | For month‑to‑month leases, landlords must give **30 days’ written notice** before raising rent. | Verify the notice is in writing and keep a copy. |
| **9** | **Lease Termination** | You can terminate a lease early under certain conditions (e.g., landlord breach, military deployment). | Review your lease for any early termination clauses; document any breaches. |
| **10** | **Discrimination Protections** | Under federal Fair Housing laws and Texas statutes, landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or other protected classes. | Report any discriminatory actions to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) or Texas Commission on Human Rights. |
| **11** | **Right to a Written Lease** | While not required for all leases, having a written agreement protects both parties. | Ask for a written lease if you’re signing a new rental agreement. |
| **12** | **Right to Withhold Rent** | If the landlord fails to maintain habitability, you may legally withhold rent until repairs are made. | Keep receipts and documentation of the withheld rent. |
| **13** | **Right to Repair & Deduct** | If the landlord fails to repair, you may repair the issue yourself and deduct the cost from your rent. | Obtain a written estimate and keep receipts. |
| **14** | **Right to a Refund of Unused Utilities** | If you move out early, you may be entitled to a refund of prepaid utilities. | Keep utility bills and receipts. |
| **15** | **Right to a Fair Lease Renewal** | Landlords cannot arbitrarily refuse to renew a lease or impose unreasonable terms. | Negotiate renewal terms in writing. |

### Quick Reference Checklist

1. **Read the lease** – note security deposit limits, notice periods, and any special clauses.  
2. **Document everything** – keep copies of notices, repair requests, and correspondence.  
3. **Know the timeline** – 30‑day notice for rent increases, 10‑day repair window, 30‑day deposit return.  
4. **Report problems** – in writing, and keep a log of responses.  
5. **Seek help if needed** – contact a local tenant association, HUD, or a lawyer if you face eviction or discrimination.

---

#### Useful Resources

| Resource | Link |
|----------|------|
| Texas Property Code (Chapter 91 – Residential Landlord‑Tenant Law) | https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/PR/htm/PR.91.htm |
| Texas Commission on Human Rights – Fair Housing | https://www.tchh.texas.gov/ |
| U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) – Fair Housing | https://www.hud.gov/ |
| Texas Tenant Association | https://www.texastenant.org/ |
| Texas Legal Services Center – Tenant Rights Guide | https://www.texaslawhelp.org/ |

Feel free to let me know if you’d like more detail on any specific right, or if you need help drafting a notice or a lease clause!
